Author Topic 1 — Overview: the CNS (brain + spinal cord; grey vs white matter; CSF; blood–brain barrier) and HOW brain damage produces disturbance. Explain the four ways nervous-system disturbance manifests (destructive/deficiency, irritative, release, compensation phenomena). Define the FOUR disturbance domains the syllabus names — cognitive, personality, behavioral, emotional — in plain language. Cover general principles: localisation vs diffuse, focal vs diffuse damage, acute vs progressive course, left vs right hemisphere specialisation. Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR CNS intro (txt ~lines 1389-1500) + Kolb. One SVG figure (CNS -> four manifestations -> four disturbance domains), .box.info Answer-flow, many <h4>, .box.key at-a-glance, exactly one .mn mnemonic.

Author Topic 2 — Cerebrovascular disorders (stroke & vascular dementia): define stroke/CVA; WHO pathological classification (subarachnoid haemorrhage, intracerebral haemorrhage, cerebral ischaemic necrosis incl vascular dementia) and clinical stage (TIA); ischaemic (thrombosis/embolism/arteriosclerosis) vs haemorrhagic; a table of stroke by artery (anterior/middle/posterior cerebral) and left vs right hemisphere syndromes (left: aphasia, apraxia, right-sided weakness; right: neglect, anosognosia, spatial/constructional deficits). Then the FOUR domains explicitly: COGNITIVE (aphasia, hemianopia, memory, attention, executive, dementia), PERSONALITY (inattention/personality change, amnesic syndromes), BEHAVIORAL (apraxia, ADL loss), EMOTIONAL (post-stroke depression, emotional lability/pseudobulbar affect, catastrophic reaction). Vascular dementia profile (stepwise, Hachinski). Assessment named in place (NIH Stroke Scale, Canadian Stroke Scale, GCS, Rankin Scale, Barthel Index, SINS, Clock Drawing; plus physical work-up: angiography, CSF, EEG, CT/MRI). Rehab: psychoeducation, Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy, gait retraining/BWSTT, VR/mirror therapy/mental imagery, speech therapy for aphasia (impairment-based vs communication-based). Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~1507-1677 + Kolb vascular section ~48846-48975. Include a by-artery/hemisphere table. All standard structural elements (Answer-flow, >=1 SVG, many <h4>, at-a-glance, one mnemonic).

Author Topic 3 — Developmental: Cerebral Palsy. Define CP (non-progressive motor disorder of the immature brain; congenital). Types table: spastic (cortex; diplegia/hemiplegia/quadriplegia/monoplegia/triplegia), athetoid/dyskinetic (basal ganglia), dystonia, ataxic (cerebellum), mixed. Primary/secondary/tertiary effects. The FOUR domains: COGNITIVE (attention span, visual problems, hearing loss, speech-language, learning, seizures/epilepsy comorbidity, intellectual impairment where present), PERSONALITY/EMOTIONAL (frustration, low self-esteem, social/emotional adjustment), BEHAVIORAL (ADL and motor-control limits, communication). Assessment tools (Ages & Stages Questionnaire, BRIGANCE Screens, Child Development Inventories/Denver II, Parents' Evaluation of Developmental Status, M-CHAT). Rehab: neurosurgical (ablative/non-ablative, segmental/suprasegmental), OT, PT (incl aqua therapy, hippotherapy), speech-language therapy, adaptive equipment/assistive tech, biofeedback, spasticity management (positioning/seating, splinting/casting, oral medication). Source: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~1678-1870. All standard structural elements.

Author Topic 4 — Degenerative: Parkinson's disease (anchor) + Alzheimer's/Huntington's for contrast. Parkinson's: dopamine loss in substantia nigra/basal ganglia; cardinal motor signs (resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia/hypokinesia, postural instability). FOUR domains: COGNITIVE (bradyphrenia/cognitive slowing, executive dysfunction, dementia in later stages, visuospatial), PERSONALITY (rigidity, apathy, impulse-control changes often dopamine-therapy related), BEHAVIORAL (hypersexuality, pathological gambling/shopping, punding, wandering), EMOTIONAL (depression, anxiety, psychosis, sleep disorders, fatigue). Contrast Alzheimer's (memory-led cortical dementia) and Huntington's (chorea + subcortical dementia + mood) briefly in a table. Shared neurodegenerative symptom profile (cognitive impairment domains, mood, psychosis, sleep, fatigue, neuro-behavioural). Assessment (PET, SPECT, MMSE & 3MSE, Hachinski Ischemic Score, Clock Drawing, Blessed Information-Memory-Concentration, ADL, Blessed Functional Assessment Scale, Geriatric Depression Scale, Neuropsychiatric Inventory-Q). Rehab/management: pharmacological (levodopa/dopamine agonists, MAO-B inhibitors, anticholinergics, cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine), cognitive rehabilitation (remedial vs compensatory), physical exercise/gait training, OT. Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~2550-2760 (neurodegenerative/infectious section) + Kolb Parkinson's refs. All standard structural elements incl a dementia-subtype comparison table.

Author Topic 5 — Trauma: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Spinal Cord Injury (SCI). TBI mechanisms: open vs closed head injury, coup/countercoup, diffuse axonal injury, haematoma/edema/raised intracranial pressure, secondary injury; severity by GCS with a scoring/severity table (and the Grade 1-4 classification from the notes). Post-concussion syndrome, post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) and retrograde amnesia. FOUR domains for TBI: COGNITIVE (mental speed, concentration, memory, executive), PERSONALITY (frontal/executive personality change), BEHAVIORAL (disinhibition, anger/temper, interpersonal change), EMOTIONAL (depression, irritability, emotional change). SCI: level & completeness (complete vs incomplete; paraplegia/tetraplegia/paraparesis/tetraparesis; 'level of injury' = lowest intact segment), physical dependence; PSYCHOLOGICAL/EMOTIONAL adjustment (depression, body-image, grief, quality of life), personality/coping. Assessment: GCS, X-ray/CT/MRI. Rehab/management: management of associated injuries, pain (CBT for pain, relaxation, biofeedback, hypnosis), memory & attention (direct attention training, external memory aids, behavior management antecedent vs consequence, learning new skills via procedural memory, metacognitive/awareness training), speech-swallowing rehab (AAC, apraxia/dysarthria, dysphagia techniques). Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~1871-2240 + Kolb head-injury section ~48976-49100. All standard structural elements incl a GCS/severity table.

Author Topic 6 — Convulsive: Epilepsy. Define (Hughlings Jackson 1889: 'occasional, excessive, disorderly discharge of nervous tissue'); causes; seizure types table — primary generalized vs focal (localization-related), with examples (petit mal/absence, tonic-clonic, etc.); the three temporal phases: aura/pre-ictal (warnings), ictal (seizure symptoms), post-ictal state. FOUR domains: COGNITIVE (ictal vs interictal vs postictal cognition, memory, attention, AED cognitive effects), PERSONALITY (the interictal personality/behaviour syndrome — temporal-lobe: hypergraphia, hyperreligiosity, viscosity, circumstantiality, altered sexuality — Bear & Fedio / Blumer; present carefully as described in literature), BEHAVIORAL (automatisms, behaviour change), EMOTIONAL (depression, anxiety, fear/panic aura, psychosis, quality of life). Assessment (EEG, ECG, blood testing, PET, spinal tap, Bender Visuo-Motor Gestalt, Luria-Nebraska Neuropsychological Battery, WADA test, serum prolactin). Management/rehab: AEDs (list the named drugs), psychotherapeutic (relaxation therapy, behaviour modification, CBT for depression, GSR & EEG biofeedback, educational interventions, family counselling). Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~2244-2430 + Kolb interictal refs. All standard structural elements incl a seizure-type table.

Author Topic 7 — Infectious: AIDS Dementia Complex / HIV-Associated Neurocognitive Disorder (HAND). Explain HIV/AIDS and how the virus reaches and damages the CNS (direct CNS infection, neuro-inflammation; subcortical dementia pattern); spell out all acronyms (HIV, AIDS, HAND, ADC, CNS). FOUR domains: COGNITIVE (psychomotor slowing, attention/concentration, memory, executive, progressing to dementia), PERSONALITY (apathy, social withdrawal), BEHAVIORAL (reduced initiative, motor slowing, gait), EMOTIONAL (depression, anxiety, stigma-related distress). Staging/severity (asymptomatic -> mild neurocognitive disorder -> HIV-associated dementia; mention memory/motor/behaviour profile). Assessment (neuropsychological screening, MMSE, functional/ADL). Rehab/management: demystifying infection, education re stigma, antiretroviral context, cognitive rehabilitation, psychosocial support. Source: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~2555-2620 (infectious + 'Demystifying Infection' + stigma education). All standard structural elements.

Author Topic 8 — Assessment: the neuropsychological assessment process and named batteries/tests. Explain WHY and the general process (history, physical/lab work-up before neuropsych testing, screening then full battery, functional/ADL assessment). Named batteries/tests explained in place via glossed-term convention, organised in a table: PGI Battery of Brain Dysfunction (PGI-BBD — standard Indian battery; describe its subtests/purpose from PGI_battery_OCR.txt if readable, else describe accurately as the Indian neuropsychological battery by Pershad & Verma), Luria-Nebraska Neuropsychological Battery, Halstead-Reitan Battery, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) & 3MSE, Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (executive/frontal), Bender Visual-Motor Gestalt Test, Clock Drawing Test, Hachinski Ischemic Score, Blessed Information-Memory-Concentration, Geriatric Depression Scale, Neuropsychiatric Inventory, Barthel Index & ADL scales, GCS, NIH/Canadian Stroke Scales, Rankin Scale. Include screening vs comprehensive and functional/ADL assessment. Sources: BM NOTES SENIOR assessment lists across the unit + PGI_battery_OCR.txt (check /projects/sandbox/work/extracted/PGI_battery_OCR.txt; if OCR is weak, describe PGI-BBD accurately without fabricating specifics). All standard structural elements incl a batteries/tests table.

Author Topic 9 — Psychological intervention & rehabilitation (cross-cutting): principles of neuro-rehabilitation (spontaneous recovery + medical rehab + learning to live with handicap; start early; multidisciplinary team). Cognitive rehabilitation (remedial/restorative vs compensatory; drill & practice, mnemonics, link method, visual story method; environmental aids). Behavioural methods (behaviour modification/ABA, antecedent vs consequence management, positive behaviour support). Psychotherapy/CBT for adjustment & depression; supportive therapy; interpersonal therapy; relaxation/biofeedback. Family & caregiver work; group therapy (education & family groups); psychosocial rehabilitation; vocational and ADL rehabilitation; therapies for comorbid anxiety/depression. Source: BM NOTES SENIOR txt ~2600-2620 (psychosocial rehabilitation + comorbid-disorder therapies) + cognitive-rehab section ~2500-2560. All standard structural elements.
